text: The point of child support guidelines is not to exactly calculate what a child needs each month. Its purpose is to approximate the share of income that would have been available for the child if the parents were living together, so that a child is not worse off because of a divorce. So, if dad makes $100,000 and mom makes $50,000, guidelines would say that if they were together, $150,000 would be available for the child. That is why the guidelines look at gross income. There's a lot of stuff that can be modified. It's a starting point, not a strict rule. But, if the child needs more, there's the concept of deviation from guidelines. I see a lot of cases where the court will deviate from guidelines in the child's interest. In fact, I think in most states, the court has the authority to deviate from the guidelines.
